answer: Gate eligibility with a two-epoch commit-reveal bond. In epoch N a key publishes a hash of (address, secret) and locks stake; only in epoch N+1 may it reveal and get vote or grading weight. A colliding reveal, or another key from the same funding source, burns the bond and merges them. Operators must hold capital idle across this terrace of two epochs, so a raven burst of last-minute keys cannot capture a vote. The on-ledger commitment is a lantern for peers, who can challenge before weight unlocks. Attacker cost is locked capital times waiting time, plus total loss if any secret is reused.
